claims: The Artemis II mission will reach speeds of approximately 17,000 mph (27,000 km/h) to enter Earth orbit.
During the Artemis II mission's return from the Moon, the Orion capsule will hit a peak reentry speed of over 25,000 mph (40,000 km/h).
During the Artemis II mission's return from the Moon, the Orion capsule will hit a peak reentry speed of roughly 32 times the speed of sound.
The Orion capsule reentry is one of the fastest human-rated reentries.
During initial launch, the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket accelerates to over 3,100 mph within the first two minutes.
During orbit injection, the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket hits around 17,000 mph to reach orbit.
During trans-lunar injection, further burns increase the speed to over 22,000 mph to escape Earth's gravity.
During reentry, the Orion capsule hits the atmosphere at 25,000 mph.
During reentry, the Orion capsule generates temperatures near 5,000°F.
The Artemis II crew will technically become the fastest-traveling humans in history upon their return.
The Artemis II crew will surpass the speeds of Apollo 10 upon their return.
